intro: In the centuries before 221 BCE, China was a land of rival states at war, and teachers traveled from court to court offering advice on how to restore order. Two of the answers they gave have lasted more than two thousand years. One, from Confucius and his followers, said order begins at home: in respect for parents, in ritual done with a sincere heart, and in rulers who lead by moral example. The other, gathered in the Daodejing and the stories of Zhuangzi, said order comes from letting go: from acting without forcing, like water that yields and yet wears away stone.

These two traditions shaped the family, the school, the government, the arts and the religious life of China, and through China much of East Asia, including Korea, Japan and Vietnam. They did not usually compete for members. The same family might keep Confucian ancestor rites, hire a Daoist priest for a healing ritual and ask Buddhist monks to chant at a funeral. That makes them a test case for the study of religion, because they do not fit a definition built around one creed and one congregation.

In this unit you will read the Analects and the Daodejing in James Legge's public-domain translations, along with the stories of Zhuangzi. You will be able to explain ren, li, xiao, the junzi, the Dao, wu wei, and yin and yang in the traditions' own terms. You will trace how Confucian texts became the curriculum of the Chinese state, how Daoism grew into a religion with priests and scriptures, and why the question of whether Confucianism is a religion still has more than one answer.
bigQuestion: What makes a good person and a well-ordered society: cultivated effort and ritual, or letting go and following the natural Way, and can one life hold both?

timeline.t: The Zhou dynasty begins and claims the Mandate of Heaven
Confucius is born in the state of Lu
Confucius dies; his followers begin compiling the Analects
Passages of the Daodejing are buried at Guodian; Zhuangzi and Mencius teach
The Legalist state of Qin unifies China
The Han Imperial Academy begins teaching the Confucian classics
Daoist tradition dates Zhang Daoling's revelation and the Celestial Masters to this year
Civil-service examinations begin under the Sui dynasty
Wang Chongyang begins the Quanzhen, or Complete Perfection, order of Daoism
The Four Books with Zhu Xi's commentaries become the examination standard
James Legge publishes his English translation of the Analects
China abolishes the civil-service examinations after thirteen centuries

words.d: the idea that Heaven grants the right to rule to a virtuous ruler and withdraws it from a cruel one
the collection of Confucius's sayings and dialogues compiled by his followers
humaneness or benevolence; the highest Confucian virtue, care for others
ritual, ceremony and proper conduct; the outward form that ren takes
filial piety: the respect, care and deference owed to parents and ancestors
the exemplary person of cultivated character; Legge's superior man
honoring and making offerings to deceased family members as continuing members of the family
the Way; in the Daodejing, the nameless source of all things and the pattern they follow
non-action or not-forcing; acting in harmony with the natural course of things
two complementary forces, dark and light, receptive and active, whose balance describes all change
vital energy or breath flowing through the body and all of nature
Confucianism, Daoism and Buddhism, long practiced side by side in China

test.q: In Zhou thought, why could a dynasty lose the Mandate of Heaven?
choices: Because the ruler became cruel and lost his virtue
Because a new king was born
Because the capital moved
Because the Daodejing was written
test.why: The mandate depended on virtue; Heaven withdrew it from cruel rulers, as the Zhou said of the last Shang king.

choices: Laozi
Confucius's followers, over generations
Sima Qian
Zhu Xi
test.why: The Analects records Confucius's sayings as preserved by his disciples and their students.

test.q: Which pair matches a Confucian term with its meaning?
choices: Ren: the uncarved block
Li: non-action
Xiao: filial piety
Junzi: vital energy
test.why: Xiao is filial piety; the uncarved block is pu and non-action is wu wei, both Daoist terms, and qi is vital energy.

test.q: What rule did Confucius give as one word to guide a whole life in Analects 15.23?
choices: Obey the ruler in all things
Seek the Way that cannot be named
Act without forcing
Reciprocity: what you do not want done to yourself, do not do to others
test.why: In Legge's translation the word is Reciprocity, stated in the negative form.

test.q: Which thinker taught that human nature is good, pointing to the child at the well?
choices: Mencius
Xunzi
Han Feizi
Zhuangzi
test.why: Mencius said anyone would feel alarm for the child, showing the inborn sprout of ren.

test.q: How did Confucian texts shape the Chinese state for about thirteen centuries?
choices: They were carved on the Great Wall
Civil-service examinations on the classics selected officials
Daoist priests read them at funerals
They were banned by every dynasty
test.why: From 605 to 1905 CE, candidates for office were tested on the Confucian classics and later the Four Books.

test.q: The Daodejing opens by saying that the Tao that can be trodden is not the enduring Tao. What is the point?
choices: The Tao is a road in the Zhou capital
The Tao can be fully defined in words
No words can fully capture the Dao
The Tao is a name for Laozi
test.why: Chapter 1 warns that naming the Dao falls short of it; the book points to what words cannot hold.

test.q: Which statement best describes wu wei?
choices: Strict ritual observance
Rule by harsh law
Complete inactivity
Effective action without forcing, like water finding its way
test.why: Wu wei is non-forcing action; the Daodejing says the Dao does nothing, yet nothing is left undone.

test.q: A Confucian and a Daoist both advise a ruler. Which advice fits the Daodejing?
choices: Govern a great state as you would cook a small fish, without constant stirring
Begin by rectifying names
Test officials on the Four Books
Build ancestral temples in every county
test.why: Chapter 60 of the Daodejing advises a light touch; the other three are Confucian measures.

test.q: What does the story of Zhuangzi's butterfly dream call into question?
choices: The value of the examinations
The sharp line between one self and another, and between dreaming and waking
Whether ancestors should be honored
Whether Laozi existed
test.why: Zhuangzi cannot tell whether he dreamed he was a butterfly or is a butterfly dreaming; the story calls it the transformation of things.

test.q: How do yin and yang relate to each other?
choices: Yin is evil and yang is good
They are two rival gods
They are complementary and turn into each other; balance is the aim
They are the two halves of the Analects
test.why: Yin and yang complete each other, like the shady and sunny sides of one hill.

test.q: Which is a feature of Daoism as an organized religion?
choices: The Mandate of Heaven
The five relationships
The civil-service examinations
Ordained priests, monastic orders and a canon of about 1,400 works
test.why: The Celestial Masters, Quanzhen monastics and the Daozang show Daoism as an organized religion.

test.q: Why do many scholars hesitate to call Confucianism simply a religion or simply a philosophy?
choices: It has Heaven, ancestral rites and temples but no creed, clergy or congregation
Its texts are lost
It was never practiced outside Lu
Confucius forbade anyone to classify it
test.why: It has religious features and lacks others, and the Chinese word for religion, zongjiao, took on that meaning only in the late 1800s.

test.q: In the Chinese Rites Controversy, what did Jesuit and Dominican missionaries disagree about?
choices: Whether to translate the Daodejing
Whether Catholic converts could keep rites honoring ancestors and Confucius
Whether to build churches in Beijing
Whether Laozi wrote the Daodejing
test.why: Jesuits called the rites civil customs; Dominicans called them idolatry; the pope banned them in the early 1700s.

test.q: A family in Chicago keeps ancestor tablets, visits a Buddhist temple at New Year and practices tai chi. What does this best show?
choices: That the family has left all three teachings
That Confucianism has replaced Buddhism
That the three teachings are often blended in practice
That tai chi is a Confucian ritual
test.why: Chinese life has long drawn on Confucian, Buddhist and Daoist practices together, a blending scholars call syncretism.

write.prompt: What makes a good leader? Write an essay that cites at least two texts from this unit, such as Analects 2.3 or 12.11 and Daodejing chapter 37 or 60. Explain what a Confucian and a Daoist would each say and why, and where their answers overlap.
tips: Name the text and passage you cite, such as Analects 12.11 or Daodejing chapter 60.
Attribute every belief: Confucius teaches, the Daodejing says, many Daoists hold.
Use the unit's terms, such as ren, li, wu wei and the Mandate of Heaven, and explain each one.
Compare the two answers without ranking them, and note where they agree.
Remember that Chinese readers often held both traditions at once.
